subject: Predicting lower, median, and upper bound dependent variable from the estimated beta coefficients

messages.author: d6a22ac7ce11aa1b
messages.subject: Predicting lower, median, and upper bound dependent variable from the estimated beta coefficients
parts:
Hi All,

I am currently working on fitting the negative binomial regression using the rstanarm package.

Next I would like to predict the dependent variable at lower (2.5%), median (50%), and upper bound (97.5%). I have no idea on how I can achieve that in rstanarm.

I will appreciate the help of everyone.

Thanks.

stan_glm1<-stan_glm(totalcrashes ~ studyperiod + majaadt + minaadt + majlane + minlane + speed + landuse + medianwidth 
                    + mediantype,
                    data = crashdata_CB,
                    family = neg_binomial_2,
                    chains = 4, 
                    seed = 123, 
                    warmup=2000, 
                    iter = 10000,
                    QR= TRUE,
                    prior = normal(0,1),
                    prior_intercept = normal(0,1))

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Predicting lower, median, and upper bound dependent variable from the estimated beta coefficients
parts:
On Saturday, October 29, 2016 at 6:36:10 PM UTC-4, malai...@gmail.com wrote:

I am currently working on fitting the negative binomial regression using the rstanarm package.

Next I would like to predict the dependent variable at lower (2.5%), median (50%), and upper bound (97.5%). I have no idea on how I can achieve that in rstanarm.

You can't because it wouldn't be a good thing. The point of posterior prediction is to integrate over the entire posterior distribution of the parameters rather than predicting given marginal quantiles of the parameters. You can look the quantiles of the posterior_predict() with summary() or quantile() or whatever.

Ben

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Predicting lower, median, and upper bound dependent variable from the estimated beta coefficients
parts:
I think we'll be introducing a function predictive_intervals that will summarize the posterior predictive distribution in the way Ben mentioned. For now you can do it in two steps with something like this:

preds <- posterior_predict(fit)
apply(preds, 2 quantile, prob = vector_of_probabilities))

posterior_predict is the most important function in rstanarm (other than the model fitting functions). It's at the core of nearly everything you'll ever need to do after fitting a model.

Hope that helps,

Jonah
